questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Demand and Its Determinants' refers to.
questions.a: Demand is the quantity of a good buyers are willing and able to purchase at a price: it rises as price falls and falls as price rises, while income, tastes, prices of related goods and expectations shift the whole demand.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Demand and Its Determinants'.
questions.a: Price down, demand up: the law of demand, with income and taste as its partners.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Demand and Its Determinants' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 9 (source: iest109.txt opening sections (factors that influence demand))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Supply and Its Determinants' refers to.
questions.a: Supply is the quantity sellers offer for sale at a price: higher prices invite larger supply, while costs of inputs, technology, number of sellers and expectations determine how much the market receives at each price.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Supply and Its Determinants'.
questions.a: Price up, supply up: sellers respond to reward, costs and technology shape capacity.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Supply and Its Determinants' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 9 (source: iest109.txt sections on supply and its factors)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Market Equilibrium - Where Price Settles' refers to.
questions.a: Demand and supply together solve the price puzzle: the equilibrium price is where quantity demanded equals quantity supplied; a price above it leaves surplus and pushes price down, a price below leaves shortage and pushes price up.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Market Equilibrium - Where Price Settles'.
questions.a: Surplus presses price down, shortage pushes it up: equilibrium is where they balance.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Market Equilibrium - Where Price Settles' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 9 (source: iest109.txt sections on equilibrium of demand and supply)
